Faridabad News: तेज धूप और उमस ने बढ़ाई परेशानी, बारिश का इंतजार
विज्ञापन
खबरें लगातार पढ़ने के लिए अमर उजाला एप डाउनलोड करें
या
वेबसाइट पर पढ़ना जारी रखने के लिए वीडियो विज्ञापन देखें
अगर आपके पास प्रीमियम मेंबरशिप है तो
अधिकतम तापमान 36 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया
संवाद न्यूज एजेंसी
फरीदाबाद। मौसम में लगातार हो रहे बदलाव के बीच शनिवार को तेज धूप और उमस ने लोगों की परेशानी बढ़ा दी। सुबह से ही धूप का असर तेज रहा। दोपहर होते-होते गर्मी और उमस के कारण लोग पसीने से बेहाल नजर आए। जरूरी काम से घरों से बाहर निकले लोगों को गर्मी का सामना करना पड़ा।
शनिवार को शहर का अधिकतम तापमान 36 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 27 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया। दोपहर के समय बाजारों और प्रमुख सड़कों पर गर्मी का असर साफ दिखाई दिया। तेज धूप के कारण दोपहिया वाहन चालकों को भी सफर के दौरान परेशानी हुई। कई लोग गर्मी से बचने के लिए पेड़-पौधों और दुकानों के बाहर बनी छांव का सहारा लेते नजर आए।
मौसम विभाग के अनुसार रविवार को भी गर्मी से राहत मिलने की संभावना कम है। रविवार को अधिकतम तापमान 35 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 27 डिग्री सेल्सियस के आसपास रहने की संभावना है। हालांकि, मौसम में बदलाव का दौर जारी रहने से बारिश की संभावना भी बनी हुई है। पिछले कुछ दिनों से शहर में कभी तेज धूप तो कभी बारिश का दौर देखने को मिल रहा है। इससे तापमान में उतार-चढ़ाव बना हुआ है। बारिश होने के बाद लोगों को उमस और गर्मी से कुछ राहत मिलती है, लेकिन धूप निकलते ही स्थिति फिर असहज हो जाती है। शहरवासियों का कहना है कि उमस ने परेशानी बढ़ा दी है। अब लोगों को अच्छी बारिश का इंतजार है, जिससे तापमान में गिरावट के साथ गर्मी और उमस से राहत मिल सके।

Fifth heat wave of summer breaks as clouds, showers and cooler air move in midweek
BAKERSFIELD, Calif. (KBAK/KBFX) — The week that was our latest was home to a heat wave, the 5th one of the summer and a dramatic weather change between Wednesday and Thursday that saw clouds increase, temperatures decrease and even some wet weather at times and in spots. Now onto the weekend...
The tropical moisture from what was once Tropical Storm Iselle is expected to be evicted out of the area by a trough of low pressure swinging in from the Pacific Northwest.
This will lead to a much quieter, sunnier and slightly warmer forecast for the weekend, locally. At this time afternoon highs on Saturday could end up right around average in the South Valley. The deserts still look hot with triple digits expected.
The good news is we are watching a sizeable cooldown for early next week.
Have a great day!
Chief Meteorologist Ilya Neyman

In a written statement issued by the Tunisian Young Doctors’ Organization, it was noted that an “unprecedented” increase had been recorded in the number of people hospitalized and those who lost their lives due to heatstroke and extreme heat in emergency rooms across various regions of the country. The statement noted that fatalities had occurred in some emergency rooms, adding that doctors and nurses were working “under pressure that exceeded the capacity of the health system” and were experiencing “extreme fatigue.”
It was noted that relevant units of the Tunisian Ministry of Health are collecting data on heat-related deaths, heatstroke cases, and intensive care unit capacity, but have not yet released official figures. The Tunisian Young Doctors’ Organization called for a “state of emergency in healthcare” due to the current situation.
In a post on his Facebook account yesterday evening, the organization’s president, Vecih Zekkar, stated that 13 people had died within 24 hours at the Habib Burgiba Hospital in the eastern city of Sfakes. Tunisian authorities have not yet released official statistics regarding deaths linked to the heat wave.
TEMPERATURE REACHED 49.8 DEGREES
During the severe heat wave that has affected much of Tunisia since Wednesday, August 26, temperatures in the central city of Kairouan were recorded at 49.8 degrees. According to data from the Tunisian Meteorological and Climate Observatory, Kairouan became the second-hottest city in the world, following Mehran, Iran, where temperatures reached 50 degrees.
The Observatory reported that six of the world’s 20 hottest locations are in Tunisia, with Kairouan, Beca, Jendouba, Gabès, Tuzer, and Zagwan among them.
POWER OUTAGES ACCOMPANY HEAT WAVE
The extreme heat wave coincided with the Tunisian Electricity and Gas Company (STEG) resuming temporary power outages in various regions of the country. STEG stated that the outages were carried out to “protect the security and sustainability of the electrical system.”
Tunisian President Kays Said also stated in a statement on Thursday, August 27, that prolonged water and power outages—which can last more than 10 hours in some regions, including the capital Tunis—“cannot be considered merely temporary incidents or isolated cases.”

articles.title: Red Alert On Junk Food: FSSAI To Flag High Salt, Sugar & Fat - Vibes Of India
articles.search_term: ("heat advisory" OR "heat action plan" OR "heat alert" OR "IMD warning" OR "IMD alert" OR "red alert" OR "orange alert" OR "yellow alert" OR "NDMA advisory" OR "cooling shelter" OR "relief measures" OR "heat compensation" OR "severe weather warning") Andaman and Nicobar Islands
articles.full_text:
Consumers may soon find a clear red warning on the front of packaged food products when they contain high levels of salt, sugar or fat. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has agreed to introduce prominent red-coloured hexagonal warning labels to make it easier for people to identify foods high in nutrients of concern.
The regulator informed the Supreme Court about its decision through a compliance affidavit filed in response to the court’s August 13 order on front-of-pack labelling (FoPL).
The proposed system is aimed at helping consumers understand important nutritional information quickly, without having to study detailed information printed on the back of a packet.
What will the new warning labels say?
Under the proposed framework, packaged food products crossing specified nutrient limits will carry clear warnings on the front of the package. Depending on their nutritional content, the warnings will read:
“HIGH FAT”
“HIGH SALT”
“HIGH SUGAR”
The labels will use a red hexagonal design, making them easy to notice while shopping.
The system is based on nutrient thresholds prescribed under the Dietary Guidelines for Indians, 2024, issued by the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR-NIN).
Single-ingredient foods to be exempted
FSSAI has proposed that certain single-ingredient foods will not have to carry these warning labels, subject to applicable food safety and labelling regulations.
These include products such as ghee, edible oil, salt, sugar, jaggery and honey.
The regulator has also proposed introducing the front-of-pack warning system in phases rather than bringing all requirements into force at once.
Two-phase implementation
Under the proposed plan:
Phase I will cover products that are high in two or more specified nutrients.
Phase II will expand the warnings to products that are high in any one specified nutrient.
The phased approach is intended to give the food industry time to make changes and, where required, reformulate products.
Why is front-of-pack labelling being introduced?
The move comes amid concerns about public health and the increasing prevalence of childhood obesity.
The Supreme Court has observed that clear front-of-pack information could help consumers make more informed purchasing decisions.
Instead of requiring shoppers to examine lengthy nutritional information, the proposed warning system would immediately highlight whether a product contains high levels of nutrients that may be a concern when consumed in excess.
FSSAI described the proposed system as a simple, prominent and easily understandable warning for consumers.
Study shows warning labels can improve identification
An India-based study involving 2,869 adults across six states tested different front-of-pack labelling systems through a randomised experiment.
The findings shown in the information provided indicate that only 39.1% of participants correctly identified all products high in sugar, saturated fat or sodium when there was no warning label.
With warning labels, the figure increased to 60.8% — an improvement of 21.7 percentage points.
The study also found that warning labels performed better than other tested systems, including traffic-light labels, GDA and Health Star Rating, in helping consumers identify foods high in nutrients of concern.
Supreme Court had asked Centre to take a decision
The development follows a PIL filed by NGO 3S and Our Health Society, which approached the Supreme Court through advocate Rajiv Shankar Dwivedi.
The petition sought front-of-pack labelling so consumers could make better-informed decisions while purchasing packaged foods.
The Supreme Court had considered several possible ways of displaying nutritional information, including coloured indicators, words, numbers, letters, symbols and percentages.
The court directed the Centre to take a decision on the issue and place it on record.
The court had also indicated that if the Union government acted on its own, it would be welcomed; otherwise, it could issue further directions.
International examples also cited
FSSAI pointed to international examples where front-of-pack warning systems have already been adopted, including Chile and Canada.
The regulator’s position is that a prominent warning on the front of a packet can help consumers recognise products with high levels of specified nutrients before making a purchase.
The proposed system now represents a significant step towards making nutritional warnings more visible on packaged food products in India, with implementation planned in phases.

articles.title: Yellow alert for storms in Buenos Aires: rains up to 40 mm and hail in Monte Hermoso and Bahía Blanca - Noticias Ambientales

articles.full_text:
The National Meteorological Service (SMN) has issued a yellow alert for storms for the province of Buenos Aires and other regions of the country this August 29. Rainfall of varying intensity is anticipated along with electrical activity, wind gusts, and possible hail.
Meanwhile, Neuquén and Río Negro are also under a yellow alert, not only for rain but also for snowfall. These conditions will persist until the night and extend into the next day.
Impact of the storms in the Province of Buenos Aires
According to the SMN, accumulated precipitation of between 15 and 40 millimeters is expected in the southwest and south of Buenos Aires, affecting areas such as Monte Hermoso, Coronel Dorrego, and Bahía Blanca. The Atlantic coast will also receive these storms, although instability is expected to decrease by nightfall.
Among the affected municipalities are San Cayetano, Necochea, and Coronel Suárez, among others. The situation, although intense, is expected to improve by tonight.
In other regions, Corrientes and Misiones also face a storm alert, with precipitation that could accumulate between 60 and 80 millimeters. In Corrientes, the phenomenon will mainly affect the west, while in Misiones it will impact more in the center and south.
The SMN recommends not leaving home during the storms or seeking shelter if outdoors. Other recommendations include not taking out the trash, cleaning drains, and securing objects that may be blown away by the wind. It is also advisable to disconnect appliances in case of flooding and close doors and windows.

A severe storm that hit various regions of France disrupted daily life. According to local sources, the storm—which began in the central parts of the country on August 27—brought winds reaching 142 kilometers per hour and heavy rain as it moved toward the eastern border.
ORANGE ALERT ISSUED IN 44 REGIONS
An orange alert was issued in 44 regions nationwide due to the storm, and various instances of property damage occurred in the capital, Paris, and its surrounding areas.Strong winds caused objects to be blown about, and numerous trees fell onto roads. Vehicles sustained damage, and pieces of roofing that broke off from some buildings fell onto the roads, posing a safety risk.
In some regions, hail the size of tennis balls fell. In many areas, particularly the cities of Besançon, Montbéliard, and Beaune, hail shattered car windows and caused disruptions to transportation. Damage was also reported on the A36 highway, which connects France to Germany and Switzerland, due to the storm and hail.
PASSENGER TRAIN WINDOW SHATTERED
Following the storm, an orange alert remained in effect yesterday in 26 regions. Videos shared on social media showed the moment a passenger train’s window shattered during the severe storm, a person struggling to walk due to the wind, and streets flooded with rising water levels after the storm. Post-storm footage also showed damage to vehicles and trees that had fallen onto roads.
